description: This topic examines the difference between weather and climate, the elements and factors that determine climate, major climate types in Africa and Tanzania, the natural vegetation types associated with them, and how human activities affect vegetation.

mcq.questionText: What is the main difference between weather and climate?

options.text: Weather refers to a short period while climate refers to a long period
Weather is measured only at night while climate is measured during the day
Weather affects oceans while climate affects only land
Weather is found in towns while climate is found in villages

mcq.explanation: Weather is the condition of the atmosphere of a place for a short time, while climate is the average weather condition of a place observed over a long period, usually 30 to 35 years.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an element of climate?
mcq.explanation: Rainfall is an element of climate because it is one of the measurable conditions of the atmosphere; latitude, altitude and distance from the sea are factors that influence climate.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
mcq.explanation: A barometer is the instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure, while a thermometer measures temperature and a rain gauge measures rainfall.

mcq.questionText: Which climate type in Africa experiences high temperatures and heavy rainfall throughout the year?
mcq.explanation: The equatorial climate, found near the equator such as in the Congo Basin, has high temperatures and heavy rainfall all year round with no distinct dry season.

mcq.questionText: The savanna climate is mainly characterized by which feature?
mcq.explanation: The savanna (tropical) climate, common in much of Tanzania, has a distinct wet season and a long dry season with moderate to high temperatures.

mcq.questionText: Why does temperature generally decrease as one climbs up a mountain?

options.text: The air becomes thinner and loses heat as altitude increases
The sun is farther from the mountain top
There is more oxygen at the top

mcq.explanation: As altitude increases, the air becomes thinner and holds less heat, so temperature falls; this is why mountain tops like Kilimanjaro are cold and may be snow-capped.

mcq.questionText: Which type of natural vegetation is dominated by tall, evergreen trees forming a thick canopy?
mcq.explanation: Tropical rainforests grow in the equatorial climate and consist of tall, evergreen, broad-leaved trees that form a continuous thick canopy.

mcq.questionText: Which vegetation type is mainly made up of grasses with scattered trees such as acacia and baobab?
mcq.explanation: Savanna grassland is characterized by tall grasses with scattered drought-resistant trees such as acacia and baobab, and it covers much of Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: How are plants in semi-desert and desert areas adapted to survive the dry conditions?

options.text: They have large, broad leaves to catch more rain
They have long roots and thorny or small leaves to reduce water loss
They grow very tall to reach the clouds
They have soft stems that store no water

mcq.explanation: Desert and semi-desert plants such as cacti are adapted by having long roots to reach deep water, and thorny or small leaves to reduce water loss through transpiration.

mcq.questionText: Which factor explains why coastal towns like Dar es Salaam have a smaller temperature range than inland areas?

options.text: The moderating influence of the sea

mcq.explanation: The sea heats and cools slowly, so coastal areas experience cooler days and warmer nights, giving them a smaller temperature range than inland areas.

mcq.questionText: What is the most direct relationship between climate and natural vegetation?

options.text: Climate has no effect on vegetation
The amount of rainfall and temperature determines the type of vegetation that grows
Vegetation determines the type of climate of an area
Only soil, not climate, controls vegetation

mcq.explanation: Climate strongly controls vegetation; areas with heavy rainfall and high temperatures support forests, while drier areas support grassland or semi-desert vegetation.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a human activity that destroys natural vegetation?
mcq.explanation: Uncontrolled bush burning destroys natural vegetation, whereas afforestation, forest reserves and replanting are conservation measures that protect vegetation.

mcq.questionText: Which line of latitude passes near the centre of the equatorial climate zone?
mcq.explanation: The equatorial climate is centred on the Equator (0 degrees latitude) where the sun is overhead for most of the year, giving high temperatures and heavy rainfall.

mcq.questionText: Why does the desert climate of the Sahara receive very little rainfall?

options.text: It is too close to large oceans
Dry descending air and distance from moisture sources prevent rain formation
It is covered by thick forests

mcq.explanation: Deserts like the Sahara lie under zones of dry, descending air and far from moist sea winds, so clouds rarely form and rainfall is very low.

mcq.questionText: Mangrove vegetation in Tanzania is mainly found in which location?

options.text: On the peaks of high mountains
Along sheltered coastlines and river mouths
In the middle of large lakes

mcq.explanation: Mangrove forests grow in salty, muddy water along sheltered coastlines and river mouths, such as the Rufiji delta on the Tanzanian coast.

fib.questionText: The average atmospheric condition of a place studied over a long period of time is called _____.
fib.explanation: Climate is the average weather of a place observed over many years, usually about 30 to 35 years.

fib.questionText: The instrument used to measure the amount of rainfall is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures the amount of rainfall received at a place over a given period.

fib.questionText: The condition of the atmosphere of a place for a short period of time is called _____.
fib.explanation: Weather changes from day to day and includes elements such as temperature, rainfall and wind for a short time.

fib.questionText: The climate found near the Equator with high temperatures and heavy rainfall all year round is the _____ climate.
fib.explanation: The equatorial climate supports tropical rainforests because of its constant high heat and heavy rainfall.

fib.questionText: Vegetation made up of grasses with scattered trees such as acacia and baobab is called _____ grassland.
fib.explanation: Savanna grassland develops in tropical areas with distinct wet and dry seasons, covering much of Tanzania.

fib.questionText: The factor of climate that explains why temperature decreases as one goes higher up a mountain is _____.
fib.explanation: As altitude increases the air becomes thinner and holds less heat, so temperatures fall.

fib.questionText: The planting of trees in an area that previously had no forest is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Afforestation increases vegetation cover and helps to conserve soil, water and the environment.

fib.questionText: The salt-tolerant forests that grow in muddy water along the Tanzanian coast are called _____ forests.
fib.explanation: Mangrove forests grow in tidal, salty and muddy conditions along sheltered coasts and river mouths.

fib.questionText: The instrument used to measure temperature is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the air is, usually in degrees Celsius.

fib.questionText: The cutting down of trees and clearing of forests without replacing them is called _____.
fib.explanation: Deforestation reduces vegetation cover and can lead to soil erosion, loss of habitats and reduced rainfall.

tf.questionText: Weather and climate mean exactly the same thing.
tf.explanation: Weather is the short-term condition of the atmosphere, while climate is the average condition over a long period.

tf.questionText: Rainfall and temperature are elements of climate.
tf.explanation: Elements of climate are the measurable conditions of the atmosphere such as rainfall, temperature, wind, humidity and pressure.

tf.questionText: Latitude is one of the factors that influence the climate of a place.
tf.explanation: Latitude affects the angle of the sun's rays, so places near the Equator are hotter than those near the poles.

tf.questionText: The equatorial climate has a long dry season with very little rainfall.
tf.explanation: The equatorial climate has heavy rainfall throughout the year and no distinct dry season.

tf.questionText: Tropical rainforests grow in areas that receive heavy rainfall and high temperatures.
tf.explanation: The hot, wet equatorial climate provides the ideal conditions for the dense, evergreen trees of the tropical rainforest.

tf.questionText: Desert plants usually have broad leaves to lose as much water as possible.
tf.explanation: Desert plants have small, thorny or waxy leaves to reduce water loss, not broad leaves.

tf.questionText: The type of natural vegetation found in an area is influenced by its climate.
tf.explanation: Climate, especially rainfall and temperature, determines whether an area has forest, grassland or semi-desert vegetation.

tf.questionText: Overgrazing and bush burning help to increase natural vegetation.
tf.explanation: Overgrazing and bush burning destroy natural vegetation and can lead to soil erosion and desertification.

tf.questionText: Areas far from the sea usually have a larger temperature range than coastal areas.
tf.explanation: The sea moderates temperature, so inland areas have hotter days and colder nights, giving a larger temperature range.

tf.questionText: Most of Tanzania experiences a savanna (tropical) climate with wet and dry seasons.
tf.explanation: Large parts of Tanzania have a savanna climate with a clear wet season and a long dry season, supporting savanna grassland.

hoq.questionText: A region near the Equator has been cleared of its dense rainforest for large-scale farming. Which of the following long-term climatic effects is most likely to result from this clearing?

options.text: An increase in local rainfall and humidity
A reduction in local rainfall and rising temperatures
No change to the local climate at all
A permanent change from equatorial to polar climate

hoq.explanation: Forests release moisture into the air through transpiration; removing them reduces local rainfall and humidity and allows temperatures to rise, showing how vegetation influences climate.

hoq.questionText: Two towns lie on the same latitude, but Town X is on the coast at sea level while Town Y is inland on a high plateau. Why is Town Y likely to be cooler than Town X?

options.text: Town Y receives weaker sunlight because of its latitude
Town Y is at a higher altitude, where the air is thinner and cooler
Town Y is closer to the sea than Town X
Town Y has more forests that block the sun completely

hoq.explanation: Since both towns share the same latitude, the difference is mainly altitude; temperature falls with increasing height, so the high inland plateau is cooler.

hoq.questionText: A farmer notices that an area which was once savanna grassland is gradually turning into bare, sandy semi-desert land after years of overgrazing and tree cutting. What is this process best described as?
hoq.explanation: Desertification is the spread of desert-like conditions into formerly productive land, often caused by overgrazing, deforestation and poor land use in dry regions.
